title: About
text:
These databases and pipelines are the result of a long-term collaboration across taxonomists, bioinformaticians, and ecologists to establish robust and user-friendly databases and pipelines for environmental identification of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF). AMF associate with 80% of plant species worldwide, impacting plant growth, survival, community structure, and ecosystem function. AMF are not one homogenous group; AMF taxa have variable impacts on their plant hosts and terrestrial ecosystem function. Still, their biodiversity is poorly understood. We hope these open databases and pipelines help increase our understanding of AMF diversity, ecology, and biogeography.
We are continuously updating the LSU database and pipeline. Currently, an ESIIL working group is supporting our continued work to (1) develop the first curated long-read AMF database, (2) build robust, open-access phylogenetic pipelines for AMF identification across major gene regions; and (3) apply these novel tools to reassess global distribution patterns of AMF. Find more information here: https://esiil.org/working-groups/amf-biogeography-diversity
Please contact us with any questions, bugs, or suggestions!

Camille Delavaux - c.delavaux@nioo.knaw.nl
Robert Ramos - robert.ramos@stonybrook.edu

title: GloDB
text:
Welcome to GloDB! Here, you can find resources related to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal (AMF) large subunit (LSU) and long-read PacBio (SSU-ITS-LSU) databases and associated pipelines. The databases rely on sequencing from culture collections, and are curated in collaboration with taxonomists. The LSU pipelines allow placement of study sequences into a LSU backbone tree to identify putative AMF (phylum Glomeromycota) as well as family and genera. These can be implemented for both operational taxonomic units (OTUs) or amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). The original pipelines are built for computing clusters, but a recent version also allows for use outside of a cluster environment.
GloDB Backbone tree. A visualization of the latest curated LSU database backbone tree, including more than 400 tips with updated taxonomy. Colors show AMF genera (with grey representing outgroups).
LSU tree from curated long-read database LongGloDB. The LSU region was extracted from the PacBio long-reads to place them into the previously developed backbone LSU tree. Colors show database groups and AMF family.

title: Pipelines
text: These pipelines allow placement of study sequences into the GloDB backbone tree for phylogenetic identification of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) at the family and genus level. All pipelines support the ASV workflow; the legacy pipeline also supports OTUs.

title: Pipelines
text:
GloDB Pipelines

Legacy Pipeline (OTU and ASV)
The legacy pipeline is the original implementation for AMF identification from environmental sequences. It supports both operational taxonomic units (OTUs) and amplicon sequence variants (ASVs), and is designed for use on computing clusters.
Source code and documentation: c383d893/AMF-LSU-Database-and-Pipeline2


ASV Pipeline (post nf-core ampliseq)






WarningWork in progress



This pipeline is under active development. Scripts and documentation may change as we finalize the workflow.


This newer pipeline improves on the legacy workflow by first using nf-core/ampliseq (v2.15.0) for initial sequence processing, including quality control, demultiplexing, dereplication, and chimera removal. After ampliseq, a series of shell scripts perform final processing steps: renaming and extracting ASVs, trimming, alignment, tree building, clade extraction, and taxonomy assignment. Tree building and phylogenetic placement are performed with standalone executables (raxml, epa-ng, gappa).
The post-ampliseq scripts include:








Step
Script(s)
Description




ASV extraction
AMFrenameASVs.sh, AMFtrimmedToASVs.sh
Extract and rename ASVs from ampliseq output


Trimming
AMFseqTrimParallel.sh
Trim reads to target regions (R1, R2 cutoffs)


Alignment
AMFalignseqs.sh
Align sequences against the reference


Tree building
AMFbuildTree.sh, AMFlaunchTrees.sh
Clean the backbone tree with gappa, then run epa-ng for phylogenetic placement and gappa for grafting


Clade extraction
AMFcladesExtract.sh
Extract study sequences into clades


Taxonomy
AMFcladeTaxonomy.sh
Assign taxonomy to clades



Environment dependencies are listed in amf_pipeline_requirements.yml (managed with pixi).
Source code and documentation: mdehollander/AMF-LSU-Database-and-Pipeline2 (ampliseq branch)
Planned development: These post-ampliseq scripts are currently executed manually in sequence. A standalone Nextflow pipeline is in development that will automate these downstream scripts into a single, reproducible workflow run after ampliseq.
